claims.text: Electrospinning can effectively produce noble metal-based high-entropy alloy three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
Electrospinning creates fine fibers that can be collected in a controlled manner.
A mixture of noble-metal precursors in a polymer solution is a suitable initial material for electrospinning.
Electrospinning followed by thermal treatment forms NM-HEA structures.
Production requires control of electrospinning voltage, collection distance, and solution concentration.
The polymer matrix stabilizes the noble-metal precursors during electrospinning.
Electrospinning generates a charged jet of polymer solution.
The charged polymer-solution jet stretches and solidifies into nanofibers.
Noble-metal precursors can be incorporated into the electrospun nanofibers.
Thermal treatment converts the incorporated noble-metal precursors into a high-entropy alloy.
The resulting NM-HEA nanoframeworks will have high surface area and distinctive structural characteristics.
High surface area and distinctive structural characteristics will enhance the catalytic properties of the NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
Conventional NM-HEA production methods may produce less-controlled structures than electrospinning.
The ability of electrospinning to achieve precise atomic control in NM-HEAs may depend on the experimental conditions.
